'''Chihdo''' was a [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Thief/Legends|thief]] who was an associate of [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Rik Duel/Legends|Rik Duel]] and [[Dani/Legends|Dani]]. He was a cousin of [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]]<ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> who somehow survived [[Navik/Legends|Navik the Red's]] [[Tetsu Clan]] purges.

==Biography==
[[File:Greedo.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Chihdo's cousin Greedo.]]
Chihdo partnered with Rik Duel and Dani some time before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] and met [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] before his involvement with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. He was also friends with the Rodian treasure hunter, [[Suz Tanwa]].<ref name="BigRedOne">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040722yavin1|series=Yavin: The Big Red One|text=Part 1: Giant}}</ref>

===The Stenax shuffle===
Shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Rik, Dani and Chihdo were operating on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] world of [[Stenos/Legends|Stenos]], where they were hired by [[Quorl Matrin]], [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]], to uncover the statue of the [[Stenax]] god [[Vol]] to expand the former [[Senator/Legends|senator's]] collection. The statue had been buried during an earthquake years earlier, causing the winged Stenaxes to stop flying in disgrace.<ref name="mc70">[[Star Wars (1977) 70|''Star Wars'' (1977) 70]]</ref>

Rik, Dani and Chihdo began digging for the statue in an old temple that had served as a Rebel Alliance base commanded by [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Pejanes Kindar|Kindar]]. Their search was interrupted when [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] arrived, along with Solo, [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. Duel claimed that he and his partners had actually joined the Rebellion and were left behind to find the Vol statue. Solo was suspicious of his old "friend", but agreed to help find the statue.<ref name="mc70" />

Eventually, after a series of double-crosses, the Rebels made their escape from Stenos, leaving Rik, Dani, Chihdo and Matrin's [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] to fend off the attacking Stenaxes, who wanted Vol returned to them.<ref name="mc70" /> Quick thinking on Rik's part allowed his gang to escape in the confusion, while Matrin was killed.<ref name="mc71">[[Star Wars (1977) 71|''Star Wars'' (1977) 71]]</ref>

===Frozen===
[[File:Chihdo_in_carbonite.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Chihdo frozen in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]], upon being captured by Bossk and IG-88C.]]
Chihdo's activities just after the Vol incident have not been documented, although it is known that he operated on Stenos with his partners and probably learned about aerodynamics to match up with the natives like Dani did.<ref name="M73">[[Star Wars (1977) 73|''Star Wars'' (1977) 73]]</ref>

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Chihdo and his partners were in Stenos. For unknown reasons, Chihdo was captured by a team of [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], including [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]] and [[IG-88C/Legends|IG-88C]], who were allied with [[Barpotomous Drebble/Legends|Barpotomous Drebble]]. Chihdo was frozen in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] and then transported through the streets. Duel and Dani were searching for his missing friend. Meanwhile, Luke Skywalker and [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] tracked Bossk and IG-88 to Stenos, believing the hunters could lead them to their missing friend Han Solo, who was also frozen in carbonite. Calrissian saw the frozen Rodian and mistook him for Solo. Calrissian and Skywalker tried to rescue Solo, only to discover that he was not Solo and that the bounty hunters were ambushing them.<ref name="mc71" />

Dani and Duel tried to rescue his friend, but the overwhelming power of the bounty hunters foiled their attempt. Eventually, with the help of a number of Stenaxes recruited by Chewbacca, the bounty hunters were defeated. Rik remained on Stenos, and Chihdo was eventually freed from the carbonite after Skywalker and Calrissian moved on to their next stop, along with stowaway Dani.<ref name="mc72">[[Star Wars (1977) 72|''Star Wars'' (1977) 72]]</ref>

===After Endor===
Within weeks after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Chihdo, Rik and Dani began looting worlds left in ruins after the Empire's retreat in the chaos following [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] death. One of their stops was water-world [[Iskalon/Legends|Iskalon's]] abandoned surface facility, [[Pavillion]]. The trio was soon interrupted by the arrival of Luke Skywalker, who had come to offer the [[Iskalonian]]s a place in the newly forming government. Luke scolded them, before they were all attacked by a hungry [[chiaki]] sea creature. A sudden attack by the Iskalonians followed. The natives no longer wanted anything to do with offworlders and the three thieves acceded to Skywalker's suggestion they all leave. Only an Iskalonian named [[Kiro]]&mdash;an old friend of Luke's&mdash;decided to go with them. Skywalker recruited Duel and the others to give Kiro passage in their ship, the [[Moonshadow (Rik Duel's)|''Moonshadow'']]. This would also give Skywalker a chance to keep them out of trouble.<ref name="mc82">[[Star Wars (1977) 82|''Star Wars'' (1977) 82]]</ref>

The group continued on to Skywalker's next diplomatic mission on [[Shawken]], where Rik, Chihdo and Dani explored the planet's ruins while Luke and Kiro met with local officials. While searching for priceless artifacts to steal, they accidentally trapped themselves in an underground chamber and triggered the countdown of an [[Shawken Device|ancient weapon]] that could theoretically destroy the entire universe. Skywalker and [[Plif/Legends|Plif]] the [[Hoojib/Legends|hoojib]] eventually freed Chihdo and the others, while Kiro's near-fatal sacrifice destroyed the machine.<ref name="MC87">[[Star Wars (1977) 87|''Star Wars'' (1977) 87]]</ref>

Chihdo and his partners then followed Skywalker back to the Alliance's temporary base on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]. During an altercation with Rebel soldiers over a card game, Chihdo was nearly killed in a fall from an [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|treetop village]]. Only Skywalker's [[The Force/Legends|Force]] abilities saved Chihdo's life.<ref name="MC90">[[Star Wars (1977) 90|''Star Wars'' (1977) 90]]</ref> The group stayed on Endor a short time longer before realizing there was little profit to be gained there. Chihdo and Rik soon departed though Dani chose to stay with the [[Alliance of Free Planets|Alliance]] in the wake of the supposed death of Kiro, who she had fallen in love with.<ref name="MC92">[[Star Wars (1977) 92|''Star Wars'' (1977) 92]]</ref><ref name="MC99">[[Star Wars (1977) 99|''Star Wars'' (1977) 99]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Chihdo was created by [[Mary Jo Duffy]], [[Kerry Gammill]] and [[Tom Palmer]]. When the comics were first published, the species name "Rodian" had not yet been coined and Chidho was sometimes referred to as "the little green guy with the antennae."<ref name="mc71" /><ref name="mc82" />

A possible source of his name is ''Chido'', a Mexican slang word indicating that something is admirable, fun or a good idea (an English equivalent would be ''rockin''').
